scope: O1 frozen long-window Oracle main-versus-repaired-branch comparison before any follow-up optimization or tracing. Not physical-router/M6 qualification.

statistics.primary: measurement cgroup usage_usec delta / successful completions inside the measurement epoch
secondary: raw CPU total and busy fraction
statistics.estimate: geometric mean of six paired fix/main CPU ratios; 95% t interval on paired log ratios, df=5, t=2.570581835636305
statistics.diagnostic: all six pair values, median, AB/BA subgroup medians, and exact 64-sign-flip p on mean paired log ratio; p is descriptive only
decision: Lower 95% ratio bound >1: CPU cost increase confirmed for this Oracle workload, even if smaller than 10%.
Lower bound >1.10: increase above 10% confirmed; point estimate >1.10 without this bound retains magnitude uncertainty.
CI crossing 1 is unresolved, not proof of noise or no regression. Conflicting median/AB/BA groups require causal follow-up.
Upper bound <1.10 can bound this tested workload below the 10% scale, but cannot establish zero regression.
No W/range filter, no all-directions requirement, no pooling request samples as independent runs.
Intervals are per scenario and rely on paired log-ratio assumptions; not familywise confidence across three scenarios.
statistics.invalid_data: Never delete, retry, replace or select windows. Preserve behavior errors and method failures. Report all analyzable values; incomplete/invalid/generator-limited scenarios cannot close the performance question.

secondary_analysis.scope: Post-run read-only secondary analysis of retained primary windows; no new load or diagnostics
interpretation_limits: Host steal is sampled from /proc/stat within each measurement epoch, excluding subsecond edge gaps. It is evidence about host availability, not a causal attribution.
cgroup total usage remains primary. User/system splits vary substantially (especially UDP); do not attribute function or syscall cause from this decomposition alone.
No windows were excluded, replaced or re-run.

interpretation.tcp_hit: Prespecified paired-log 95% interval is entirely above one: CPU increase confirmed for this Oracle workload. Geometric mean +12.2424%, interval +0.0135% to +25.9666%; the lower endpoint is barely positive. AB median +0.0960% versus BA +16.0316% and descriptive sign-flip p=0.09375 motivate causal follow-up. The magnitude exceeding 10% is not confirmed.
interpretation.udp_miss: Geometric mean +1.7814%, interval -4.7285% to +8.7362%; six-pair median +1.1409%. This does not reproduce the earlier +15.06% point estimate and places the per-scenario 95% upper bound below that 13-18% scale, but does not prove zero regression. AB median -3.4111% versus BA +1.4472% conflicts in direction; do not dismiss it as noise without investigation.
interpretation.dhcp: Geometric mean +0.1026%, interval -1.9846% to +2.2341%; no confirmed cost increase. The earlier +13.58% point estimate is not reproduced at this tested workload, but this is not proof of exactly equal cost.
interpretation.cpu_split: TCP hit mean delta +4.6100 us/query decomposes to user -1.3726 and system +5.9827. UDP and DHCP user/system splits vary widely; decomposition alone does not establish a syscall or userspace cause.
interpretation.host: No cgroup throttling, all ten-second idle CPU observations zero. CPU0 steal maximum 0.15270%; TCP main/fix maxima 0.00861%/0.01858%. Low observed steal is not a causal proof. Boundary lag maximum 5.382121 ms; send-lag p95 maximum 103.406 us.
interpretation.integrity: All 36 windows retained, no retries, exclusions or substitutions. Tracing/build/test loads did not run concurrently. Formal CPU values come from cgroup usage, without idle subtraction.

limits: Six pairs per scenario; confidence intervals are marginal per scenario, not simultaneous across three scenarios.
Main uses static ET_EXEC and the repaired branch static PIE; release flags otherwise match after source-path normalization. The result measures the cumulative branch, not one isolated patch.
No target router, saturation ceiling, multi-rate scan or long-term leak qualification. Traced follow-ups must be reported separately and cannot replace these primary data.
